source_refs.note: Topic 2.7.1, printed page 34: shell capacities and shell configurations.

blocks.text: The electronic configuration of an atom can also describe the distribution of electrons in its shells. The shells K, L, M, N and so on correspond to the principal quantum number n of the orbitals, and each has a specific capacity: the K shell (n = 1) holds 2 electrons at most (the 1s orbital), the L shell (n = 2) 8 (2s and 2p), the M shell (n = 3) 18 (3s, 3p and 3d), and the N shell (n = 4) 32 (4s, 4p, 4d and 4f).
